messages:
alex: Heads up — canary saw a big prefetched KV cache hit-rate drop right after the kernel-routing switch + tokenizer bump. Hit went 72% -> ~ Forty-something percent. :thinking:

miriam: whoa, can you drop the timeframe and the run id?

alex: 10:03 UTC, run id 2415-canary. warmup-bot posted the eviction spikes. See logs: warmup-bot: eviction spike at 10:04, sample keys show different serialized probes.

devon: initial hypothesis: serialization changed (tool/function field ordering) + tokenizer token ids changed -> cache key mismatch.

cheng: also possible kernel routing changed batching behaviour — shorter batches -> different prefix lengths in memcache keys (we key on first N tokens + tool signature).

sam: I pulled the trace. Perf profiler shows tokenization time per request unchanged, but KV lookup miss ratio increased from 28% -> 59%. GPU util steady. So not a pure perf regression, it's a logical keying change.

miriam: can you paste a couple of example (root) serializations?

alex: here are two adjacent requests (before vs after routing):
```
BEFORE: {"prompt":"Get user id...","tools":[{"name":"search","args":[]},{"name":"format","args":[]} ] }
AFTER:  {"prompt":"Get user id...","tools":[{"name":"format","args":[]},{"name":"search","args":[]} ] }
```

miriam: yep tool order changed. That will flip JSON text and hash. And tokenizer upgrade might have changed tokenization of system prompt whitespace -> different prefix tokens.

devon: two prongs then: 1) canonicalize tool order in key derivation, 2) pin tokenizer version for warmup cohort or add tokenizer version into the key. Which should be fast?

cheng: canonicalize tool order is lowest risk and should give immediate recovery for older clients. Adding tokenizer version into the key is safer long term but needs rollout.

sam: can we avoid invalidating entire cache by mapping old keys -> new keys for a grace period? warmup-bot: warming migration started (batch size 2000)

miriam: plan: patch keygen to sort tools and use stable separators, add tokenizer-version tag to key (but as an additive suffix so existing keys still match if we don't require it). Also add rekey-migration job to copy hot prefixes for 12h.

alex: patch in progress: https://git.redwood/s/eng/runtime/PR-ops/patch-2415 (draft). small code snippet in patch: 
```
# keygen snippet
def canonicalize_for_key(prompt_str, tools, tokenizer_v):
  p = normalize_whitespace(prompt_str).strip()
  tools_sorted = sorted(tools, key=lambda t: t['name'])
  payload = f"p:{p}|tools:{json.dumps(tools_sorted,separators=(',',':'))}|tkv:{tokenizer_v}"
  return sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()
```

devon: small nit: use stable JSON dump and explicitly exclude ephemeral tool metadata (last_used_ts, session_id). Those were leaking into keys too.

miriam: agreed, filter tool metadata. Also add unit test that simulates tokenizer v bump + reordering -> same canonical key after sort.

sam: ops: run migration job now? warmup-bot: migration job queued as JOB-PR-2415 with batch=2k, parallel=8.

alex: rolled patch to canary, pinned tokenizer to v2.1 in canary runtime flags. Monitoring: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/prefetch-hit-rate?run=2415  (live)

miriam: early telemetry: hit-rate climbed 58% -> 81% in last 20m after canonicalization + pin. GPU latency stable. Good sign.

cheng: follow-ups: 1) add tooling to diff canonical keys for a prompt set (to catch future tokenizer bumps), 2) include tokenizer version in rollout docs, 3) add alert if hit-rate drops >10% in 5m.

alex: filing follow-up tickets: SP-3421 (diff tool for keys), SP-3422 (alert), SP-3423 (rekey migration infra).

miriam: thanks team. small retrospective: kernel routing change exposed an underspecified key contract. We should treat cache key format as a stable contract in public release notes. :eyes:

devon: PR merged to canary, will monitor. If warmup job finishes and hot keys are copied, we expect >90% recovery by EOD.

sam: update: warmup job processed 18k hot prefixes, warmup-bot: copied 18,212 keys, collisions 3.

alex: else nothing urgent. closing thread once dashboards confirm recovery. :party:
